16.0.0 write compatibility

This comparison covers the pinned trees above, not the current release candidate. It measured 4,916 writes; 2,947 differed from v15.0.9. The three BF-225 cells below were fixed in #8888 and #8890. #8890 also shipped compatibility decisions A and B; #8892 later added the resend settings and merged as 3c773ee5. Its default-mode matrix differed in 0 of 4,916 cells from its base, f54941b5. That result is not a refreshed v15.0.9 comparison; the table below remains limited to the pinned trees.

Living page. Measured 2026-10-31 with the write-contract matrix (tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js) on v15.0.9 c6a0d8ed (release baseline), dev 37b2280f (pre-identity baseline), #8879 6960bfb7 (identity branch measurement).

Defaults only (WRITE_VALIDATION off, WRITE_IDENTIFIER lenient, WRITE_DELETED_EDIT ignore, UUID_HANDLING on) Node 22.23.4, MongoDB 7.0.43, two runs per tree.

Rendered from the committed data in releases/cgm-remote-monitor-16.0.0/compat/, last changed 2026-11-01 at cdf0b9659; a new measurement refreshes it by the steps in the comparison's README. Part of the 16.0.0 release record. All records in the matrix are synthetic test data.

BF-225: fixed before the current dev

The pinned #8879 tree stored a second treatment when a socket re-send omitted an identifier present on the stored record. The three affected cells are included in this measurement. #8888 and #8890 fixed the defect; it is not an open finding on current dev.

Why the count is large

The matrix tests each write form and path. Identifier-format forms account for most measured differences; these totals describe only the pinned trees.

#8879 onlyalready on devdev, then #8879

The differing cells grouped by what happens to the data. "Paths" counts distinct collection and re-send path pairs, a better measure of how many separate behaviours changed than the cell count. "Undo" is what an operator could use to get 15.0.9's behaviour back today. "Could restore" names the decision cards below whose alternative would bring this kind of change back toward 15.0.9.

Decisions that could restore compatibility

Each card records a measured compatibility alternative and its effect on the pinned comparison. Current implementation status is shown in the card. Sorted by cost (near zero, low, high), then by cells restored; the bars share one scale, up to 1,387 cells.

AAdoptedcost to the objectives: near zero

Compatibility A (#8890): API v3 refuses blank and numeric identifiers by default; other malformed identifiers remain absent/lenient.

118 cells
Alternative
Restore the earlier lenient API v3 handling for blank and numeric identifiers; this would give up the 118 measured compatibility restorations.
What it restores
The 118 identifier-format cells where v15.0.9 refused a blank (78) or numeric (40) identifier. Corrected 2026-10-31: the card first counted 349, but 231 of those were placeholders v15.0.9 stored and only refused on a later re-send as an identity change; refusing them would be a new refusal, not a restoration.
Cost
None to compatibility: no client can depend on acceptance that v15.0.9 refused. Refusing every malformed identifier on API v3 was measured against a strict run and would move at least 72 cells further from v15.0.9 (empty, JSON null and placeholders that v15.0.9 accepted), and a 400 can stall an uploader that only bounds retries on 404 (AndroidAPS, read). WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict stays the opt-in broader refusal on API v3 and the socket.
Recommendation
Shipped in #8890; strict mode remains the broader opt-in.
Maintainer decision
Shipped in #8890: API v3 refuses blank and numeric identifiers by default; WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict remains the broader opt-in refusal. (maintainer, 2026-10-31)
Kinds of change
f
BAdoptedcost to the objectives: low

Compatibility B (#8890): a matched re-send replaces the stored record on every collection and path; explicit edits keep their route-specific merge behavior.

136 cells
Alternative
Set WRITE_RESEND=merge-except-treatments to restore merge-on-re-send behavior for the collections covered by this card.
What it restores
Every replace-becomes-merge cell: profile 61, entries 25, food 22, device status 13, settings 10, activity 5; re-sent over API v3 90, socket 36, in-process 10.
Cost
Slice 4's reason applies unchanged: clients re-send whole records and clear a field by leaving it out, so under merge a cleared field stays set. Identifier-first matching, the duplicate avoidance and the unique index are unaffected. What is lost is the same as on 15.0.9: a field added on the site is dropped when the client re-sends its record. Clients found: AndroidAPS NSClientV3 settings, the web profile editor's saves.
Recommendation
Shipped in #8890; WRITE_RESEND=merge-except-treatments is the opt-in alternative.
Maintainer decision
Default replace behavior shipped in #8890; merge-on-re-send is an opt-in site mode in #8892. (maintainer, 2026-10-31)
Kinds of change
c1
CAdoptedcost to the objectives: low

58 cells
Alternative
Use WRITE_RESEND and WRITE_DELETED_RESEND to select the measured resend behavior; per-client D20 overrides remain future work.
What it restores
Opt-in: d1 28 and d2 21 (stays deleted), c2 9 (socket re-send now written); b 402 only if a mode keeps adding a second record, which no one has asked for.

Maintainer decision

DNot taken upcost to the objectives: low

Decision B and slice 6 (2026-10-31): a socket treatment re-send matched by identifier replaces; a device status re-send merges

9 cells
Alternative
A socket re-send that matches is acknowledged and nothing is written, as 15.0.9 kept the stored record.
What it restores
Socket device status 5, socket treatments 4.
Cost
Edits over the socket go through dbUpdate, not a re-send, so few clients lose anything. Decided today for consistency with slice 4; both choices are defensible.
Recommendation
Default replace behavior shipped in #8890; WRITE_RESEND=acknowledge selects this measured no-write alternative.
Maintainer decision
The default replace behavior shipped in #8890; WRITE_RESEND=acknowledge restores the measured no-write option. (maintainer, 2026-10-31)
Kinds of change
c2
EKeptcost to the objectives: high

ID-Q6: a placeholder identifier is not stored

1,387 cells
Alternative
Store the placeholder value as sent, but never match on it.
What it restores
The 1,387 cells whose only difference is that the placeholder value is no longer stored.
Cost
The unique index on identifier would then refuse the second record carrying the same placeholder, which is the case two apps sharing 'undefined' hit. Excluding placeholder strings from a partial index is not expressible in MongoDB's partial filter. No surveyed client sends a placeholder, so the compatibility gain is on paper only.
Recommendation
Keep the decision.
Maintainer decision
Agreed: keep the decision; the placeholder value is not stored. (maintainer, 2026-10-31)
Kinds of change
f
FKeptcost to the objectives: high

Where the changes land

Each square is one kind of change on one collection and re-send path. Darker means more cells. Empty means no change there. Select a square to list its cells below.

Triage: what to look at first

One row per kind of change, collection and re-send path. Score = severity of the worst effect (1 to 10; bug fixes and avoided duplicates capped at 3, the defect at 10) times the number of clients read or measured as sending that shape, or half the severity where no client was found. Evidence: "measured" is a run against a server, "read" is from the client's code with file and line. Nothing is assumed.

What this cannot see

  • The results are not a post-#8890 or post-#8892 comparison.
  • Field-level and nested merge behavior, null handling, and races without the unique index were not measured.
  • A live and deleted record sharing one identifier, or an edit whose _id and identifier name different records, were not measured.
  • Re-sends after delete keyed by syncIdentifier, id or uuid were not measured.
  • Non-default settings and the unique index were not run.
  • Client shapes were read from code; only nightscout-connect was run against a server.

How to read the verdicts

  • Defect unplanned behavior in the pinned comparison; fixed on current dev as noted.
  • Decided an intentional behavior change
  • Bug fix a defect or data-loss behavior that was fixed in a later compared tree.
  • No value change the write takes another path; stored values do not change.
  • WRITE_RESEND and WRITE_DELETED_RESEND are implemented in #8892. Per-client D20 overrides remain unimplemented. The unique index is tracked separately in #8894 and was not measured here.
